arxiv-2212-00625.title: Probabilistic Neural Circuits leveraging AI-Enhanced Codesign for Random Number Generation
arxiv-2212-00625.creator: Suma G. Cardwell 1 , Catherine D. Schuman 3 J. Darby Smith 1 , Karan Patel 3 , Jaesuk Kwon 2 , Samuel Liu 2 , Christopher Allemang 1 , Shashank Misra 1 , Jean Anne Incorvia 2 and James B. Aimone 1
arxiv-2212-00625.description: Abstract Stochasticity is ubiquitous in the world around us. However, our predominant computing paradigm is deterministic. Random number generation (RNG) can be a computationally inefficient operation in this system especially for larger workloads. Our work leverages the underlying physics of emerging devices to develop probabilistic neural circuits for RNGs from a given distribution.

arxiv-2305-19169.title: Exploring interacting chiral spin chains in terms of black hole physics
arxiv-2305-19169.creator: Ewan Forbes, Matthew D. Horner, Andrew Hallam, Joseph Barker, Jiannis K. Pachos
arxiv-2305-19169.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ewan Forbes, Matthew D. Horner, Andrew Hallam, Joseph Barker, Jiannis K. Pachos. In this paper we explore the properties of a 1-dimensional spin chain in the presence of chiral interactions, focusing on the system’s transition to distinct chiral phases for various values of the chiral coupling. By employing the mean field theory approximation we establish a connection between this chiral system and a Dirac particle in the curved spacetime of a black hole.

arxiv-2312-11271.title: Active flux for triangular meshes for compressible flows problems
arxiv-2312-11271.creator: Rémi Abgrall, Jianfang Lin, Yongle Liu
arxiv-2312-11271.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rémi Abgrall, Jianfang Lin, Yongle Liu. In this article, we show how to construct a numerical method for solving hyperbolic problems, whether linear or non-linear, using a continuous representation of the variables and their mean value in each triangular element. This type of approach has already been introduced by Roe, and others, in the multi-dimensional framework under the name of Active Flux, see [ 11 , 12 , 10 , 16 , 7 ] .

arxiv-2312-16645.title: Hochschild cohomology of the second kind: Koszul duality and Morita invariance Thanks: This work was partially supported by EPSRC grant EP/T029455/1. The second author acknowledges support by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) through EXC 2121 “Quantum Universe” –
arxiv-2312-16645.creator: A. Guan, J. Holstein, A. Lazarev
arxiv-2312-16645.description: Abstract . We define Hochschild cohomology of the second kind for differential graded (dg) or curved algebras as a derived functor in a compactly generated derived category of the second kind, and show that it is invariant under Morita equivalence of the second kind.

arxiv-2401-15764.title: Improvements of readout signal integrity in mid-infrared superconducting nanowire single photon detectors
arxiv-2401-15764.creator: Sahil R. Patel, Marco Colangelo, Andrew D. Beyer, Gregor G. Taylor, Jason P. Allmaras, Emma E. Wollman, Matthew D. Shaw, Karl K. Berggren, Boris Korzh
arxiv-2401-15764.description: Abstract Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) with high timing resolution and low background counts in the mid infrared (MIR) have the potential to open up numerous opportunities in fields such as exoplanet searches, direct dark matter detection, physical chemistry, and remote sensing.

arxiv-2403-17157.title: Output-feedback Synthesis Orbit Geometry: Quotient Manifolds and LQG Direct Policy Optimization
arxiv-2403-17157.creator: Spencer Kraisler, Mehran Mesbahi
arxiv-2403-17157.description: Abstract We consider direct policy optimization for the linear-quadratic Gaussian (LQG) setting. Over the past few years, it has been recognized that the landscape of dynamic output-feedback controllers of relevance to LQG has an intricate geometry, particularly pertaining to the existence of degenerate stationary points, that hinders gradient methods.

arxiv-2410-11911.title: Transfer Learning Adapts to Changing PSD in Gravitational Wave Data
arxiv-2410-11911.creator: Beka Modrekiladze
arxiv-2410-11911.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Beka Modrekiladze. The detection of gravitational waves has opened unparalleled opportunities for observing the universe, particularly through the study of black hole inspirals. These events serve as unique laboratories to explore the laws of physics under conditions of extreme energies. However, significant noise in gravitational wave (GW) data from observatories such as Advanced LIGO and Virgo poses major challenges in signal identification.

arxiv-2410-16118.title: Simulating quantum emitters in arbitrary photonic environments using FDTD: beyond the semi-classical regime
arxiv-2410-16118.creator: Qingyi Zhou, S. Ali Hassani Gangaraj, Ming Zhou, Zongfu Yu
arxiv-2410-16118.description: Abstract We propose a numerical algorithm that integrates quantum two-level systems into the finite-difference time-domain framework for simulating quantum emitters in arbitrary 3D photonic environments. Conventional semi-classical methods struggle with these systems due to spurious self-interactions that arise when a two-level system is driven by its own radiation field.

arxiv-2410-18365.title: How High a Field Can Be and Has Been Achieved in Superconducting Bulk Niobium Cavities Across Different RRR Values?
arxiv-2410-18365.creator: Takayuki Kubo
arxiv-2410-18365.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Takayuki Kubo. This Brief Note explores the relationship between residual resistivity ratio (RRR) and the maximum surface magnetic field in superconducting bulk niobium (Nb) cavities. Data from the 1980s to 2020s, covering RRR values from 30 to 500, are compared with theoretical performance limits, including the lower critical field ( B c ​ 1 B_{c1} ), superheating field ( B sh B_{\rm sh} ), and thermal runaway field ( B run B_{\rm run} ).

arxiv-2502-00179.title: Benchmarking Quantum Instruments
arxiv-2502-00179.creator: Darian McLaren, Matthew A. Graydon, Ali Mahmoud, Joel J. Wallman
arxiv-2502-00179.description: Abstract Quantum measurements with feed-forward are crucial components of fault-tolerant quantum computers. We show how the error rate of such a measurement can be directly estimated by fitting the probability that successive randomly compiled measurements all return the ideal outcome.

arxiv-2508-19724.title: NLKI: A lightweight Natural Language Knowledge Integration Framework for Improving Small VLMs in Commonsense VQA Tasks Thanks: Now at Google
arxiv-2508-19724.creator: Aritra Dutta, Swapnanil Mukherjee, Deepanway Ghosal, Somak Aditya
arxiv-2508-19724.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aritra Dutta, Swapnanil Mukherjee, Deepanway Ghosal, Somak Aditya. Commonsense visual–question answering often hinges on knowledge that is missing from the image or the question. Small vision-language models (sVLMs) such as ViLT, VisualBERT and FLAVA therefore lag behind their larger generative counterparts.

pmc-10605630.creator: Claudio Cherchi, Elena Chiappini, Maria Beatrice Chiarini Testa, Paolo Banfi, Edvige Veneselli, Renato Cutrera, Maurizio Elia
pmc-10605630.description: Background: The purpose of this study is to better understand the way caregivers of patients with Rett syndrome perceive the quality of the health care services they receive and identify its main shortcomings. Methods: A survey was distributed to all caregivers who are part of AIRETT (the Italian Association of Relatives of Patients with RS).

BackgroundCompelling evidence supports the role of childhood traumatization in the etiology of psychiatric disorders, including adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (aADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD). The aim of this study was to examine the psychometric properties of the Hungarian version of the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire Short Form (H-CTQ-SF) and to investigate the differences between patients diagnosed with aADHD and BPD in terms of early traumatization.MethodsAltogether 765 (mean age = 32.8 years, 67.7% women) patients and control subjects were enrolled from different areas

pmc-11387577.title: GMP-compliant automated radiosynthesis of [18F] SynVesT-1 for PET imaging of synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2 A (SV2A)
pmc-11387577.creator: Lijuan Chen, Xiaochen Li, Yao Ge, Huiqiang Li, Ruili Li, Xiaosheng Song, Jianfei Liang, Weifeng Zhang, Xiaona Li, Xiaoqi Wang, Yunjuan Wang, Yaping Wu, Yan Bai, Meiyun Wang
pmc-11387577.description: BackgroundA novel positron emission tomography (PET) imaging tracer, [18F] SynVesT-1, targeting synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2 (SV2A), has been developed to meet clinical demand. Utilizing the Trasis AllinOne-36 (AIO) module, we’ve automated synthesis to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards, ensuring sterile, pyrogen-free production.

pmc-11602432.title: Sobrerol in Managing Acute Respiratory Infections in Clinical Practice During the “Cold” Season: An Italian Primary Care Experience
pmc-11602432.creator: Attilio Varricchio, Giorgio Ciprandi, On behalf of the Study Group on respiratory infection management in clinical practice, Francesco Paolo Brunese, Francesco Paolo Brunese, Luigi Costanzo, Lorenzo Cresta, Maurizio Daccò, Donatella Del Gaizo, Carla Dominici, Cosimo Lanza, Michele Lisco, Anastasia M
pmc-11602432.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeAcute upper respiratory infections (AURI) represent a daily challenge in primary care practice. Mucus production may impair during AURI. Sobrerol is a muco-active agent that improves rheological characteristics and exerts other ancillary activities.

pmc-11749258.title: Tmem88 plays an essential role in pharyngeal pouch progenitor specification by inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling
pmc-11749258.creator: Jingwen Liu, Liping Yang, Zidong Lu, Qiang Wang
pmc-11749258.description: Pharyngeal pouches, which are endodermal outpockets that segment the pharyngeal arches, play a crucial role in the development of craniofacial skeletons in vertebrate embryos. Our previous study successfully identified pharyngeal pouch progenitors (PPPs) in zebrafish embryos and emphasized the significance of BMP2b signaling in their specification.

pmc-12395685.title: Amygdala volume abnormalities and cognitive impairment in major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder II
pmc-12395685.creator: Bin Li, Chunguo Zhang, Wensheng Chen, Guojun Xie, Jiaquan Liang
pmc-12395685.description: BackgroundThe amygdala, as a crucial brain region, plays a key role in processing emotions and cognitive information. Given that patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder II (BD II) experience cognitive impairments, accurate diagnosis becomes a vital research focus.

pmc-13424429.title: Development of economic selection indexes for beef-on-dairy systems and implication for sire re-ranking in U.S. production systems
pmc-13424429.creator: Larissa E Meier, Bruce L Golden, Scott Newman, Matthew L Spangler
pmc-13424429.description: The rapid expansion of beef-on-dairy (B×D) crossbreeding in the United States has increased the need for selection tools tailored to this unique production system. The objectives of this study were to develop economic selection indexes specific to B×D systems under U.S. conditions and to evaluate the extent of sire re-ranking relative to conventional beef-on-beef (B×B) indexes.

pmc-13602593.title: Angiocrine factors in tumor microenvironment: bidirectional crosstalk, mechanistic insights, and therapeutic strategies
pmc-13602593.creator: Gaili Ji, Yaping Wang, Xiaoxue Li, Zuchen Yang, Luyao Kang, Yutian Chen, Caixia Ma
pmc-13602593.description: BackgroundTumor recurrence, metastasis, and treatment resistance represent core challenges in clinical oncology closely associated with the complex and dynamic tumor microenvironment (TME). Endothelial cells (ECs), key components of the TME, have functions that extend far beyond the traditional concept of tumor angiogenesis. In recent years, extensive research has revealed that ECs perform endocrine and paracrine functions by secreting angiocrine factors.

pmc-13615171.title: Acute high‐protein feeding induces hepatic amino acid accumulation in diabetic male mice prior to transcriptional adaptation
pmc-13615171.creator: Hiroaki Sumioki, Eisuke Tomatsu, Yusuke Seino, Shihomi Hidaka, Shinji Ueno, Sayumi Kanie, Koki Nishida, Takuya Haraguchi, Naoya Murao, Haruki Fujisawa, Takeshi Takayanagi, Yoshihisa Sugimura, Yoshitaka Hayashi, Atsushi Suzuki
pmc-13615171.description: Glucagon plays a pivotal role in hepatic amino acid metabolism; acute high‐protein diet feeding and diabetic condition both induce enhanced glucagon secretion. However, it remains unknown whether these two conditions alter hepatic amino acid metabolism through the same or different pathways.

pmc-13651166.title: Transcranial photobiomodulation improves prefrontal oxygenation and impulse control in adults with ADHD: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13651166.creator: Farzad Salehpour, Douglas W. Barrett, Anagh Mirji, Ayla Farzamnia, Vikas Burugu, Nisarg Shah, Francisco Gonzalez-Lima
pmc-13651166.description: BackgroundImpulsivity in individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diminishes quality of life. Cortical hypometabolism has been hypothesized to contribute to ADHD. Transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) is a safe, non-invasive method for stimulating the prefrontal cortex (PFC), yet its cognition-enhancing effect on impulsivity and sustained attention in adults with ADHD remains understudied.
